scope: Internal same-binary ZINC prefill A/B on the Intel Arc Pro B70; no competitor win or release qualification
limitations: The prototype replaces exactly one generic prefill SPV in the same packaged binary. Production adopts the bit-identical kernel under a separate Intel shader name and a qualified dense-Q8 model gate.
The renamed source changes comments only; the same remote compiler produced a shader bitwise identical to the numerical and A/B candidate.

Three balanced rounds retain every warmup and measured request, complete output hashes/token counts and natural EOS. Prefill improves in every workload/round; decode is unchanged within measurement variation.

The numerical gate compares full-vocabulary last-token logits against serial GPU F32-KV inference at 14 token boundaries per arm. Actual A/B requests use F16 KV and native continuations before/after each server.
These results do not establish a llama.cpp win, an all-model gain, or startup/memory/streaming-latency improvements.
The production CI archive and dispatch/fallback validation are separate from this same-binary prototype.
